name: Mathematics
fwnote: Codes are Common Core State Standards for Mathematics identifiers (e.g. 2.NBT.B.5, HSA-REI.B.4), adopted by Illinois in 2010 as its Learning Standards for Mathematics; HSN-CN.C.9 is a (+) advanced standard. The alignment is the course author's judgment and is not a certification.

1.bq: How do numbers tell us how many, and why do we group things in tens?
std: K.CC.A.1
Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
K.CC.B.4
Pair each object with one number name and understand the last number said tells how many.
K.CC.C.6
Decide whether one group has more, fewer or the same number of objects as another.
1.NBT.B.2
See a two-digit number as some tens and some ones, with ten as a bundle of ten ones.
1.NBT.B.3
Compare two two-digit numbers by their tens and ones using >, = and <.
1.NBT.C.5
Mentally find ten more or ten less than a two-digit number and explain why.

2.bq: How do we put numbers together, take them apart, and know the answer is right?
std: K.OA.A.1
Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, drawings, acting out, verbal explanations, expressions or equations.
Solve add-and-subtract word problems within 20 with the unknown in any position.

Understand that the equal sign means both sides are the same amount.
Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100 involving addition and subtraction.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently, knowing sums of two one-digit numbers from memory.
2.write: Mia has 7 stickers. She gets 6 more. Then she gives 4 to a friend. How many stickers does Mia have now? Solve it one step at a time. Then check your answer a second way.

ch.bq: How do numbers change when we put groups together or take some away?

Is 4 + 2 = 6 true? What happens to the scale after you take a block off?
How many marbles did your friend drop in? Write the sentence with a ? for the missing number.
What pattern do you see in the sums? What would 6 + 6 be?

ch.bq: What tricks help you know adding and subtracting facts fast?
ch.talk: Why do the three numbers in the house make exactly four facts?
ch.story: The Fact House on the Wall

Write the four facts on the door for 5, 7 and 12.
How many cups do you have at the end? Check it a second way.

3.bq: How do hundreds, tens and ones let us count, compare, add and subtract numbers up to 1,000?
std: 2.NBT.A.1
Understand a three-digit number as amounts of hundreds, tens and ones.
2.NBT.A.3
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.

Compare two three-digit numbers by place value using >, = and <.
2.NBT.B.5
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value and properties of operations.
2.NBT.B.7
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and drawings, regrouping when needed.

ch.bq: How can three little digits stand for a number as big as 1,000?
ch.talk: Why did making groups of ten help Kai and Rosa count faster than counting one by one?

Which tower is worth more, and what place did you check to decide?
Which sign belongs in 720 ? 702: greater than, less than or equal to?
How many buttons would 7 cups hold? Keep the pattern going.
What floor is 100 more than 384? What floor is 200 less than 384?
Is 23 even or odd? Is 24 even or odd? How do you know?

ch.bq: How do hundreds, tens and ones help us add and subtract big numbers?

What is 324 + 153? What does your drawing show?
If the pattern keeps going, how many cups on Friday? What about Saturday?
Why does moving 1 from 44 to 29 keep the total the same?

4.bq: How do we use numbers to say how long, what time and how much?
std: Measure a length by laying same-size units end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Measure lengths choosing suitable tools such as rulers, yardsticks and meter sticks.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, using a.m. and p.m.
Solve word problems with dollars, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.
Measure lengths and show the data on a line plot.
Make picture graphs and bar graphs and answer questions from them.
4.write: You have one quarter, two dimes and one nickel. You buy a cookie for 35¢. How much money do you have? How much is left after you buy the cookie? Explain each step.
rooms: Length, time and money — cards, quiz and lab

ch.bq: How can we measure how long something is and show what we found?
ch.talk: Why did Amir and Nia get different numbers for the same hallway?

l.look: Which pencil is longer? How do you know?
Which stick is in the middle when you put them in order?
Whose measurement is right? Why?
How many inches are in 2 feet? How do you know?
Why is the centimeter number bigger than the inch number?
A desk looks like 3 rulers long. About how many inches is that?
How many more votes did dog get than fish?
How many pencils are shorter than 7 inches?

ch.bq: How do clocks and coins help us know what time it is and how much we have?

How many nickels make one quarter?
How much money is in the hand? Now count it a second way to check.
How much does Priya spend? Did she pay the right amount?
How much change does Sam get? Check it with subtraction.

5.bq: How do we name a shape, and how do we cut it so every share is fair?
std: K.G.A.2
Name shapes correctly no matter their size or how they are turned.
Tell defining attributes such as sides and corners from non-defining ones like color or size.
Put together two- and three-dimensional shapes to make new shapes.
Recognize and draw shapes with given attributes, such as a number of angles or equal faces, and name them.
Divide a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count them.
Partition circles and rectangles into halves, thirds and fourths and describe the equal shares.
5.write: Three friends want to share one square brownie fairly. Draw how you would cut it. Then tell what each friend gets and how you know the shares are equal.
rooms: Shapes and equal shares — cards, quiz and lab

ch.talk: Look around your room right now. What is one shape you can see, and how do you know its name?

Which two shapes have the same number of sides? How can you tell them apart?

Which solid has the most flat faces? Which has none? Which one could you not stand a cup on?

What did Jon draw? What did Ava draw? Could both drawings be right?
Name the shape of the door, the roof and the clock. Which solid shape is a trash can?

ch.bq: What makes a share fair, and how can we cut a shape so every share is the same?
ch.talk: Ben cut the sandwich into two pieces. Why was that still not fair? What did the second cut do differently?

Who has more brownie, Mia or Jon? How do you know?
How many cuts make thirds? How many cuts would you need for five equal pieces?
Which cut gives the smallest slice? Which cut gives the biggest? Why?
What pattern do you see as you add a row? How many squares would 5 rows of 4 have?
What is each cousin's share called? What could the aunt have done if she knew five cousins were coming?

6.bq: How do multiplication and division work together to count, share and check the world around us?
6.bqe: ¿Cómo trabajan juntas la multiplicación y la división para contar, repartir y comprobar el mundo que nos rodea?
std: Interpret a product of whole numbers as a number of equal groups.
Interpret a quotient as sharing into equal groups or finding how many groups.
Use the commutative, associative and distributive properties to multiply and divide.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently, knowing single-digit products from memory.
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations and check answers by estimating.
Solve multi-step word problems with whole numbers, interpreting any remainder.
6.write: Solve this problem and explain each step: A camp has 26 campers. Each tent holds 4 campers. How many tents does the camp need? Then explain how you know your answer is right, and what would change if the question asked how many campers are in the last tent.
6.writee: Resuelve este problema y explica cada paso: Un campamento tiene 26 niños. En cada tienda caben 4 niños. ¿Cuántas tiendas necesita el campamento? Luego explica cómo sabes que tu respuesta es correcta, y qué cambiaría si la pregunta fuera cuántos niños hay en la última tienda.
rooms: Multiplication and division: what they mean — cards, quiz and lab

What do you get each way? Do the digits of your answer add to 9?
How much does each product grow by? Do the products switch between odd and even? Why?
How many juice packs are in one box? In 4 boxes? Show both multiplications.

ch.bq: When you split a total into equal parts, how do you know how many each part gets, and what happens to the leftovers?

How many full rows are there, and how many students sit in the last row?
How many tents are needed? How many campers sleep in the last tent?
How many students are there? How many juice packs are needed? Show both steps.
What are the two answers? Which operation did you do first in each one?
Which estimates are higher than the exact answer, and which are lower? Why?

7.bq: How do ten digits and their places let us count, compare, and compute with numbers too big to picture?
std: 4.NBT.A.1
Recognize that each place is ten times the value of the place to its right.
4.NBT.A.2
Read, write and compare multi-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form.
4.NBT.A.3
Use place-value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
4.NBT.B.4
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
4.NBT.B.5
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two two-digit numbers, using place value, arrays and area models.
5.NBT.B.6
Divide whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, explaining the method.

8.bq: How can numbers describe amounts that fall between the whole numbers, and how do those numbers behave when we add, compare, multiply and divide them?
8.bqe: ¿Cómo pueden los números describir cantidades que quedan entre los números enteros, y cómo se comportan esos números cuando los sumamos, los comparamos, los multiplicamos y los dividimos?
std: Represent fractions as points on a number line built from unit fractions.
Explain fraction equivalence and compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including in word problems.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by finding equivalent fractions.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number or a fraction, using area models.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions with models and stories.
8.write: A recipe calls for 3/4 cup of sugar. You want to make 2 1/2 batches. Find how much sugar you need, then explain each step so a classmate could follow it. Before you finish, predict whether the answer should be more or less than 3/4 cup, and check your work a second way.

Antes de terminar, predice si la respuesta debe ser más o menos que 3/4 de taza, y revisa tu trabajo de una segunda manera.
